ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is the power supply; the upper end of the power supply is connected to the upper branch, and the upper branch is connected to the upper plate of the capacitor; the lower branch passes through a component labeled “computer” and then is connected to the lower plate of the capacitor. The capacitor is fixed on the outer frame, and between the two plates there is a movable dielectric. The right side of the dielectric is connected to the part labeled “mass block,” and the right side of the mass block is further connected to a light spring, which is fixed on the right outer frame. Reasoning: When the sensor suddenly accelerates to the right from rest, due to inertia, the mass block has a tendency to move left relative to the outer frame, and drives the dielectric on the left side to move left deeper between the capacitor plates. The deeper insertion of the dielectric increases the capacitance of the capacitor. The power supply voltage remains unchanged; from Q=CU it can be known that when the capacitance C increases, the charge Q carried by the capacitor increases, so the capacitor is in the charging process. In the figure, the positive terminal of the power supply is connected to the upper branch. During charging, the conventional current flows from the positive terminal of the power supply along the upper branch to the upper plate of the capacitor, and then returns to the negative terminal of the power supply through the lower branch of the external circuit via the “computer”; its circulating direction is clockwise.
